scenario: A ski-resort investors' brief features only resorts that remain solvent and maintain winter occupancy above 85%. Investors use the highlighted average occupancy to estimate typical occupancy across all resorts.

data.description: Only surviving resorts with occupancy above 85% are featured. Occupancy is Normal with sigma 10 percentage points.

question: Estimate (a) the true mean occupancy mu across all resorts and (b) the fraction of resorts featured.
naive_answer: Typical occupancy is about 90.3% because that is the highlighted average.
naive_trap: The brief covers only exceptionally strong surviving resorts.
reasoning_trace: Solving the truncated-normal equation gives mu≈75 and featured fraction≈0.1587.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(85-mu)/10; return mu+10*norm.pdf(a)/norm.sf(a)-90.25
mu=brentq(eq,0,84.99)
frac=norm.sf((85-mu)/10)
assert abs(mu-75)<1 and abs(frac-0.1587)<0.005
